name: XS-AUTOCORR: cross-sectional autocorrelation-regime book (trend on predicted-persistent, anti-trend on predicted-anti-persistent residual returns, beta-hedged, 5-day stride), with the regime forecast learned from OHLC/hourly roughness + multi-day VR pooled across the 273-asset PIT panel
mechanism:
DATA FLOW. From the 1-minute `ohlcv` table, one streaming pass per asset (the existing `trader/data.py:145-187` `aggregate_asset_daily` already yields (day, open, high, low, close, volume, trade_count); `build_daily_panel_from_db` at `:190-226` then discards O/H/L and keeps only `c` at `:205-207` — extend it to return H/L/O panels, and add an hourly key so the same pass also emits 24 hourly closes/day). Per asset-day, compute: log daily return r (close-to-close), Parkinson σ²_P=(ln H/L)²/(4 ln 2), Garman–Klass σ²_GK=0.5(ln H/L)²−(2ln2−1)(ln C/O)², Rogers–Satchell σ²_RS=ln(H/C)ln(H/O)+ln(L/C)ln(L/O), realised variance from 24 hourly returns RV_1h=Σ_h r_h², n_traded_minutes/1440, dollar volume, and a Corwin–Schultz spread proxy from 1-day vs 2-day ranges. On a 24/7 venue the Yang–Zhang overnight term ln(O_t/C_{t−1}) is the one-minute gap between 23:59 and 00:00 (≈0 unless the asset did not print) so YZ degenerates to k·σ²_OC+(1−k)·σ²_RS; the overnight/intraday split is meaningless here and is replaced by (a) the UTC-boundary-free hourly RV and (b) weekday/weekend sub-ranges as optional features. Market factor = equal-weight (or dollar-volume-weight) daily return of live assets; residual returns e_i=r_i−β̂_i r_mkt with β̂ from a trailing 90d causal regression. Windowed over W=28 days (4 weeks, kills weekly seasonality), the per-asset REGIME FEATURES are: IVR=mean_W(r²)/mean_W(RV_1h) (the Lo–MacKinlay VR(24) at hourly→daily aggregation, >1 ⇔ intraday persistence), RR=mean_W(r²)/mean_W(σ²_P) and its GK/RS twins (the OHLC-native analogue: under Brownian motion E[σ²_P]=σ² so RR=1; a persistent/smooth path has small range relative to its close-to-close move ⇒ RR>1; anti-persistent ⇒ RR<1), multi-day VR_i(q) for q∈{5,10,30} on RESIDUAL returns over 180d (Lo–MacKinlay overlapping, bias-corrected), Kaufman efficiency ratio |C_t−C_{t−30}|/Σ|ΔC| on residual log-price, trailing realised trend-efficiency ȳ over the last 4 non-overlapping 90d windows (the NO-LEARNING baseline predictor), β̂, idio-variance share, dollar-volume rank, n_traded fraction, CS spread. TARGET: y_{i,t}=Σ_{u=t+1}^{t+90} sign(E_30,i,u−1)·e_{i,u}/(σ̂_i√90), the forward 90-day realised PnL, in vol units, of the fixed rule "sign of the trailing 30-day cumulative RESIDUAL return, held one day" — i.e. the exact quantity the book harvests (a first-order estimate of A_30=Σ_{k=1}^{30}ρ_i(k), the same object as VR(30)−1 up to weights; Dao et al. 2016), cross-sectionally demeaned per date so the learned object is the cross-sectional regime, not the market-wide one. A secondary target, forward VR_i(30), is logged for interpretability only. LEARNED OBJECT: f_θ(features_{i,t})→E[y_{i,t}], pooled over all PIT assets × dates (≈240 live × ≈1600 days ≈ 380k asset-days from 2022, ≈4k effectively independent because the target overlaps 90 days), ridge (closed form, primary) and a LightGBM with monotone constraints on IVR/RR/VR (secondary, the only nonlinear/interaction arm), expanding-window refit each quarter, 90-day purge between train end and test start; loss = MSE on the per-date-standardised y (Spearman rank objective as a reported variant). No neural nets, no policy, no value function, no search: the price transition is exogenous, the only controlled state is inventory with known dynamics, so the decision is a static map (memo §2).

CONTROL LAW. At each stride date (H=5 days): s_i=clip(ŷ_i/κ_t,−1,+1) with κ_t the cross-sectional sd of ŷ on that date, dead-zone |ŷ_i|<0.5κ_t ⇒ s_i=0 (concentrates gross on confident regimes, raising vol per unit gross, which is what makes cost survivable — see math). Raw weight w_i=s_i·sign(E_30,i,t)·1/Σ_j|s_j| (gross 1; s_i>0 ⇒ trend, s_i<0 ⇒ anti-trend on the SAME 30-day residual signal, so the two "rules" are one rule with a signed intensity). β-hedge: w←w−β̂·(Σ_j w_jβ̂_j)/(Σ_jβ̂_j²), renormalise Σ|w|=1; the book is market-neutral by construction (BEAR-agnostic, not BEAR-positive). Hysteresis on the trend sign: a flip of sign(E_30) is acted on only if |E_30|>θ·σ̂√30 with θ=0.25 (tactics-panel execution row, fixed a priori); s_i is updated only at strides; between strides hold SHARES (no constant-dollar re-trim — the 830 SPEC found daily re-trims cost BEAR22 gross, `experiments/830_corridor/SPEC.md:95-98`, and `trader/backtest.regime_series` at H=5 reads exactly this: pos on the stride grid × 5-day forward log return, `trader/backtest.py:205-228`). Fallback: if <20 assets clear the dead-zone, keep the previous book and log the event. EXECUTION: rebalance at the UTC-midnight close of the stride day, cost 21 bp/side on Σ|Δw| (`trader/backtest.py:188-190`), graded by unmodified `cell_metrics` (`:231`) at H=5 on the PIT true-daily panel; a maker/limit layer is not part of the mechanism (907's estimands are second-order at this turnover). Optional arm C (NOT BEAR-agnostic, pre-registered as a fallback only): s_i∈[0,1] — persistence-weighted trend with no anti-trend leg — which keeps the directional trend book's 65%-vol cost economics but inherits its 2024–26 gross≈0 unless a persistent subset exists.
math:
(1) Regime statistic. VR_i(q)=Var(Σ_{k=1}^q r)/(qσ_i²)=1+2Σ_{k=1}^{q−1}(1−k/q)ρ_i(k). Lo–MacKinlay iid-null sd of the overlapping estimator ≈ sqrt(2(2q−1)(q−1)/(3qn)): q=30,n=365 ⇒ 2·59·29/(90·365)=0.104 ⇒ sd 0.32; q=30,n=90 ⇒ sd 0.65; q=5,n=365 ⇒ sd 0.14. A per-asset multi-day VR(30) is therefore unusable as a per-asset estimate on any window shorter than several years — the reason to (a) pool across 273 assets and (b) use the intraday statistics, which have ~1440 observations/day. Range bias: for a random walk observed at N discrete points/day, E[range_N]≈E[range_cont]·(1−0.73/√N) (Broadie–Glasserman–Kou continuity constant β=0.5826 applied to max and min), so σ²_P is biased down ≈3.8% at N=1440, ≈14% at N=100 traded minutes, ≈25% at N=30 — common-mode for liquid names, but correlated with illiquidity, hence the n_traded control. Bid-ask bounce inflates the range (H=ask prints, L=bid prints) ⇒ RR biased DOWN for wide-spread names ⇒ they look anti-persistent; Corwin–Schultz separates it (spread component equal in 1-day and 2-day ranges, variance doubles). Under fBm with Hurst H, VR(q)=q^{2H−1} and E[range²]/Var(X_T) is a decreasing function of H (=4ln2 at H=½), so RR and IVR are monotone in H IF self-similarity holds from 1h to 30d — an assumption the pre-test P2 measures rather than assumes.

(2) Rule payoff. Sign-trend rule w=sign(R_T), R_T=Σ_{k=0}^{T−1}r_{t−k}: for Gaussian (R_T, r_{t+1}), E[w·r_{t+1}]=√(2/π)·Cov(R_T,r_{t+1})/sd(R_T)=√(2/π)·σ·A_T/√(T·VR(T)) with A_T=Σ_{k=1}^Tρ(k); Var≈σ². Annualised per-asset Sharpe SR_i≈√365·0.798·A_T/√T=2.78·A_30 at T=30. Flat ρ over 30 lags ⇒ VR(30)−1≈A_30 ⇒ SR_i≈2.78(VR−1); AR(1) fast decay ⇒ VR−1≈2A ⇒ SR_i≈1.39(VR−1); so SR_i∈[1.4,2.8]·(VR_i(30)−1). Dao et al.: linear rule expected gain per day (λ/2)σ²(VR(T)−1) — same object, different weights. Record check: 819 PIT FULL gross +0.74 (POWERED_RESULT.md RESULT table) with N_eff~8 ⇒ mean A_30≈0.74/(2.78·2.83)=0.094 over 2018–25; BULL24/CHOP25 gross +0.13/+0.22 ⇒ mean A_30≈0 in 2024–25. The record measured the MEAN of A_30 across assets, never its cross-sectional DISPERSION.

(3) Book. E[gross SR]≈0.798·ρ_f·sd_true(SR_i)·√N_eff, ρ_f=corr_cs(forecast, TRUE SR_i). Reliability from the persistence pre-test: y (90d realised trend-efficiency) has noise sd 1 and E[y]=SR_ann·√90/√365=0.497·SR_ann; if ρ̄=corr_cs(y_w,y_{w+1}) then sd_true(y)=sqrt(ρ̄/(1−ρ̄)), sd_true(SR_ann)=2.01·sqrt(ρ̄/(1−ρ̄)): ρ̄=0.05→0.46, 0.10→0.67, 0.20→1.0. Forecast from m=4 past windows (true value constant, optimistic): ρ_f=sqrt(mρ̄/(1−ρ̄+mρ̄)): ρ̄=0.10→0.575. Then per-asset harvested SR=0.798·0.575·0.67=0.31; book gross SR=0.31√N_eff: N_eff 8→0.87, 15→1.19, 30→1.68.

(4) Cost — the binding constraint. A β-neutral book with Σ|w|=1 over N equal-|w| names with idiosyncratic daily sd ≈4% has vol 0.04/√N·√365: N=100→7.6%/yr, N=40→12%/yr, N=20→17%/yr — versus the directional trend book's 65%/yr (POWERED deployable metrics: 11.65%/yr drag @21bp = 0.18 Sharpe ⇒ vol 65%). Turnover: sign-flip probability of a T-day sum over a stride H is arccos((T−H)/T)/π: T=30,H=1 ⇒ 0.0824/day ⇒ Σ|Δw| 0.165/day (matches the measured 0.152–0.162 and the tactics panel's analytic 0.165); H=5 ⇒ 0.186 per 5d = 0.037/day ⇒ turnover 0.075/day; with θ=0.25σ√T hysteresis ≈0.06/day. Cost at 21 bp: 0.075·365·21bp=5.7%/yr ⇒ Sharpe drag 5.7/12=0.48 at N=40 (0.75 at N=100; 2.7 if run daily at N=100 — a daily-rebalanced neutral book at gross 1 is dead at 21 bp regardless of forecast quality). Requirement at N=40 (N_eff≈20–25): gross SR ≥ 0.97+0.48=1.45 ⇒ ρ_f·sd_true(SR_ann) ≥ 1.45/(0.798·√22)=0.39 ⇒ with ρ_f≈0.6, sd_true≥0.65 ⇒ ρ̄≥0.10. In VR units: sd_cs(VR(30)−1)≈0.65/2.0≈0.3 (0.23 under the flat-ρ coefficient, 0.46 under AR(1)) — assets at ±1 sd must have residual VR(30)≈0.7 and 1.3, persistently, in liquid names. That is the magnitude of Lo–MacKinlay's small-stock weekly VR anomaly, required on residual crypto returns.

(5) Multiplicity. Annualised-SR SE over the 2.5-yr 2024-01→2026-06 window ≈1/√2.5=0.63 regardless of stride. SR0(N)=E[max SR_N|H0]≈0.63·[(1−γ)Φ⁻¹(1−1/N)+γΦ⁻¹(1−1/(Ne))]: N=2→0.36, N=8→0.9, N=50→1.4. The design has 2 estimator cells + 1 baseline (N=3, SR0≈0.5); the bar +0.97 is only 1.5 SE above zero on that window, so CI lo>0 and 2026H1-alone positivity, not the point estimate, carry the verdict.
profit_source: FORECAST — of a second-moment/autocorrelation functional, not of direction: the sign and magnitude of A_30,i=Σ_{k=1}^{30}ρ_i(k) of each asset's market-RESIDUAL daily returns over the coming 90 days (equivalently VR_i(30)−1), harvested by a fixed sign-trend rule whose expected PnL is √(2/π)σ_iA_30,i/√30 per day (Dao et al. 2016 decomposition). The direction of each position comes from a public, unforecast statistic (sign of the trailing 30-day residual return); the learned object only decides whether to run that sign forward (persistent) or backward (anti-persistent) and how much. Not a risk premium (β≈0 by the hedge step, and a neutral book carries no crypto beta to be paid for); not a rebalancing premium (the engine sums constituent log returns, `trader/backtest.py:221-223` per the tactics panel, so it cannot even see one); cost reduction (H=5 stride, hysteresis, hold-shares) is a multiplier applied to whatever the forecast delivers, not a source — it is included because the math shows a neutral daily book at 21 bp is infeasible without it.
why_learning: (a) Parameter sharing across 273 assets × time is the only way to estimate the regime mapping at all: a per-asset VR(30) on a year of data has sd 0.32, the same order as the largest plausible true dispersion, so a per-asset closed-form estimator (trailing VR, trailing trend PnL) has reliability ≤~0.3; pooling ≈380k asset-days lets the mapping from ~15 roughness/liquidity/β features to forward trend-efficiency be fitted with ~100× the information, then applied to every asset including newly listed ones with short histories (PIT universe, dead coins retained). (b) The mapping is an interaction by construction: stale-price/nontrading autocorrelation (Lo–MacKinlay 1988 nontrading model) manufactures apparent persistence that is NOT tradeable, and bid-ask bounce manufactures apparent anti-persistence in the range ratio; "persistent AND liquid" and "RR after conditioning on spread and n_traded" are conjunctive/interaction terms — a monotone-constrained GBM or a ridge on engineered partials, not a raw VR, is the estimator of the harvestable component. (c) The cross-scale bridge (1h/OHLC roughness → 1–30d autocorrelation) has a closed form only under fBm self-similarity, which minute-scale microstructure (E-3: minute-scale mean reversion IC 0.15) says is violated at the short end; the functional form has to be learned, and the design pre-registers the no-learning control (trailing 4-window realised trend efficiency ȳ) that the learned arm must beat by ≥0.2 net Sharpe or be declared inert. What learning cannot do: create dispersion or persistence that is not in the panel — the pre-test P1 measures that first, with zero fitting.

bear_positive.argument: The β-hedged book is BEAR-AGNOSTIC by construction (net market exposure hedged at every stride, printed daily), so it is positive in a bear iff its net edge is positive — the requirement is transferred from the market's sign to the forecast's IC, exactly as memo §1.2 A-3 argues. It gives up the one bear-positive behaviour the record has (the 819 short leg: BEAR22 gross +1.22 PIT, LEDGER 898 baseline +1.095 vs long-flat −2.471), which was a market-level persistence read, not a cross-sectional one. BEAR22 is in-sample for any model trained from 2019, so the BEAR22 number is a form check only; the unseen test is 2026H1 (a −1.66 net@8 period for the trend book). Two conditions must hold beyond edge>cost: (i) the short leg (≈50% of gross, permanently) must be financeable — the record models no borrow cost; if Kraken spot-margin rollover is ≈0.01–0.02%/4h (recalled, unverified) that is 22–44%/yr on the short notional ⇒ 11–22%/yr on the book, larger than the trading cost and larger than a 12%-vol book's gross return at SR 1.5 — which would kill every dollar-neutral spot design before the forecast question is reached; (ii) arm C (persistence-weighted trend, no anti-trend leg) is BEAR-positive only through the trend short leg, i.e. only if the persistent subset is net short in the bear — a forecast again.

guards: 887 adaptive HOLD collapse: there is no learned policy and no reward-shaped loop to find the flat fixed point — the forecast is a regression, positions are a deterministic map, and Σ|w|=1 is enforced whenever ≥20 assets clear the dead-zone; the fallback (hold previous book) is logged per stride and >30% fallback strides on 2024-01→2026-06 is a pre-registered FAIL, as is median gross <0.5 or any >95%-flat stride. 892 re-trim damage: positions change only through (a) hysteresis-gated sign flips of the 30d residual signal, (b) s_i updates at the 5-day stride, (c) renormalisation on listing/delisting; no daily constant-dollar re-trim (hold shares between strides, native to `cell_metrics` at H=5); the turnover decomposition flip/intensity/renormalisation is printed, and pre-registered turnover >0.10/day is a FAIL (the design is dead at that turnover by the cost arithmetic). 813 selection luck: ONE pre-registered configuration (T=30, W=28, K=90, H=5, θ=0.25, dead-zone 0.5κ, 2 estimators + 1 baseline = N=3 cells, SR0(3)≈0.5 reported beside every number); no grid, no metric shopping (additions are new rows); walk-forward quarterly refits from 2019 with a 90-day purge; two placebo families with 200 draws each — asset-label permutation of ŷ within each date (destroys cross-sectional information, keeps the market regime and turnover) and circular time-shift of ŷ by ≥180 days (destroys timing, keeps per-asset marginals); PASS requires the real book above the 97.5th percentile of both. Liquidity confound (the specific luck this angle invites): partial ICs controlling n_traded, dollar-volume rank and CS spread are the reported statistics, and the book is graded with and without the bottom liquidity tercile; a PASS that disappears ex-bottom-tercile is recorded as a stale-price artifact. Multiplicity across the row: 3 cells × 1 window, N_eff of the residual panel measured (TASK_825's (Σλ)²/Σλ²), not assumed; MinBTL is trivially satisfied at N=3 but stated.

The 898 verdict kills the market-level regime as a standalone bet; the cross-sectional regime is unmeasured.

controllability: High, by construction. Two deterministic maps and one ≤15-feature regression: every position is (predicted regime intensity s_i, printable with its feature contributions — ridge coefficients or GBM SHAP) × (sign of the trailing 30-day residual return, a public statistic) × a β-hedge. Turnover is bounded a priori by the stride and hysteresis (analytic 0.06–0.075/day) and decomposed in the log; net market exposure is hedged and printed each stride; the fallback (hold previous book) is a logged event, so 887's attractor becomes a visible counter rather than a silent fixed point. Refits are quarterly, so the deployable artifact is a coefficient table plus a feature spec (a bill of materials, per the tactics panel's criterion), not a checkpoint; the whole book can be recomputed from the daily/hourly aggregates in seconds and audited against `trader.backtest.cell_metrics` with the 882 two-instrument discipline if an in-env read is wanted. Failure modes are equally legible: a PASS that vanishes ex-bottom-liquidity-tercile is a stale-price artifact; a learned arm that does not beat the trailing-ȳ baseline by 0.2 is inert learning and the mechanism collapses to a persistence rule.
compute: CPU only; no GPU at any stage, 24 GB or 64 GB cards irrelevant. Stage 0 bulk cost is one streaming pass over the 273 PIT assets' minute rows to emit daily O/H/L/C/V/trade_count plus 24 hourly closes per day — the same pattern as `trader/data.py:145-187` with an hourly key — ≈2–4 CPU-hours on gpu-server (wrapped, per `.claude/rules/10-compute-allocation.md`), cached once to a small table (≈273 × 2800 × 30 floats ≈ 180 MB). Feature panel 2800 days × 273 assets × ~15 features ≈ 11M floats (<100 MB RAM). Ridge refits: closed form, seconds; LightGBM at 380k rows × 15 features ≈ 1 min per refit × 18 quarterly refits; 400 placebo books through `cell_metrics` with n_boot 2000 ≈ 1–2 CPU-hours. Whole row < 1 CPU-day; kill date 10 days from SPEC commit.

kill_experiment.design: STAGE 0 — pre-tests, zero fitting (hours). On the PIT 273-asset true-daily panel (build_pit_universe, data.py:426; apply_liquidity_filter zf<0.15, :82), residual returns vs the equal-weight market (90d causal β), 2019-01→2026-06 cut into 30 non-overlapping 90-day windows. P1 (load-bearing, the CROSS-SECTIONAL persistence test): per window compute y_i = 90-day realised PnL of sign(trailing 30d residual return) in vol units, demeaned per window; ρ̄ = mean over consecutive window pairs of the cross-sectional Spearman corr(y_w, y_{w+1}) with Newey–West SE; null = 1000 asset-label permutations; report separately for 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025–26H1 and ex-bottom-liquidity-tercile. P2 (the OHLC content): per date, cross-sectional Spearman IC of trailing-28d IVR, RR(P/GK/RS) and residual VR(5/10/30) against the FORWARD y, raw and partial on n_traded fraction, dollar-volume rank, Corwin–Schultz spread; NW t with lag 90. P3: the market-level time-series version (tactics row 3) as a reported side statistic. Also report N_eff=(Σλ)²/Σλ² of the residual-return correlation spectrum by year (TASK_825). STAGE 1 — walk-forward book (≤1 CPU-day), only if P1 passes: train from 2019-01, test 2022-01→2026-06 with quarterly expanding refits and a 90-day purge; arms A ridge (primary), B monotone-GBM (secondary), C no-learning baseline (trailing 4-window ȳ); control law as specified (H=5, θ=0.25, dead-zone 0.5κ, β-hedge, hold shares); graded by unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics at costs (0,8,21) bp with n_boot 2000 and block ≥ 90 days; 200 asset-label-permutation placebos and 200 circular time-shift (≥180d) placebos of ŷ through the identical control law; turnover decomposition, fallback-stride fraction, gross vol, net exposure printed; secondary read of arm C' (persistence-weighted trend, no anti-trend leg) reported, never pooled. Binding window for the verdict: 2024-01→2026-06; 2026H1 alone reported as the unseen sub-period.

honest_odds: P(P1 passes at ρ̄ ≥ 0.10 with liquidity controls, 2024–26H1 included) ≈ 20–25% — crypto Hurst literature reports time-varying persistence but mostly in early, illiquid years, and Lo–MacKinlay 1990 says cross-sectional profits in equities came from lead-lag rather than own-autocorrelation. P(OHLC/hourly roughness carries partial IC ≥ 0.05 | P1) ≈ 30% — self-similarity from 1h to 30d is contradicted at the short end by the record's own minute-scale mean reversion. P(goalposts | P1 pass) ≈ 15–20% — the cost/vol arithmetic needs gross SR ≈ 1.45 on a 12%-vol book, every input at its favourable value. Unconditional P(net@21 ≥ +0.97, CI lo > 0, 2026H1 > 0, PIT) ≈ 4–5%; P(marginal +0.56) ≈ 8–10%. If the operator's Kraken tier is a maker tier (8–12 bp), the cost drag halves and these roughly double; if spot-margin rollover on the short leg is what I recall (0.01–0.02%/4h), the neutral design is dead on financing before any of this and only arm C' (not BEAR-agnostic) survives, at ≈2–3%. What the row buys regardless of outcome: the first measurement of cross-sectional dispersion and persistence of trend efficiency on the PIT panel, N_eff of the residual panel (TASK_825), and the cost-per-unit-vol fact for neutral daily books, which bears directly on TASK_915's G-B conversion.
open_doubts: Cost per unit vol is the binding constraint and the record has not priced it: a β-neutral book with Σ|w| ≤ 1 has vol ≈8–17%/yr (idio sd 4%/day over 20–100 names), so the SAME 0.15/day turnover that costs the 65%-vol directional trend book 0.18 Sharpe costs a neutral book 1.5–2.7 Sharpe; at H=5 with hysteresis it is still 0.5–0.75. This applies to TASK_915's Gârleanu–Pedersen book too (memo §4.2's 'net = gross − turnover·21bp/σ_book' with a small σ_book) and should be stated in its SPEC.

Borrow/financing of the permanent 50% short leg is unmodelled everywhere in the record; if Kraken spot-margin rollover is ≈0.01–0.02% per 4 h (recalled, unverified), the short leg costs 22–44%/yr of its notional — fatal for any dollar-neutral spot book on this venue. Writing the actual margin/rollover schedule down alongside the fee tier (loops panel point 1) is a zero-cost prerequisite.

Stale-price/nontrading autocorrelation (Lo–MacKinlay 1988) produces untradeable apparent persistence; the 819 filter (zero DAILY returns < 15%) does not exclude a coin that prints in 40 minutes/day. The n_traded and spread controls are essential and may remove most of whatever dispersion P1 finds.

Lead-lag (BTC → alts) is a cross-autocovariance term (Lo–MacKinlay 1990) that a per-asset VR does not see; residualising on the contemporaneous market removes the same-day component but a lagged-market term in the residual trend signal could carry or destroy part of the payoff — sign unknown, to be read from the market-level arm P3.

Self-similarity is the bridge from OHLC/hourly roughness to 1–30d autocorrelation and is known to fail at the minute end (bid-ask bounce; E-3's minute-scale mean reversion). P2 may pass only through liquidity proxies, in which case the 'OHLC-native' content is a spread/liquidity read, not a regime read.

The 90-day overlapping target leaves ≈4k effectively independent observations for ≈15 features; GBM overfit is likely and ridge may be the only honest arm; a single pre-registered K=90 (chosen from the 30d rule's turnover timescale) may be the wrong regime lifetime, and there is no sweep by design.

Cross-sectional VR dispersion of the required size (residual VR(30) ≈0.7 vs 1.3 at ±1 sd, persistent, in liquid names) is as large as the classic small-stock weekly anomaly; no verified paper shows such dispersion is forecastable in crypto, and the WebSearch budget was exhausted this session so the literature list marks recalled items explicitly.

The UTC-midnight day boundary is arbitrary on a 24/7 venue; daily ranges depend on it, and the weekly liquidity seasonality (weekend ranges) is a common-mode factor — the hourly-RV construction and the 28-day window are mitigations, not proofs.
N_eff of the residual panel (8? 30?) is unmeasured (TASK_825 parked) and every gross-SR number above scales with its square root.
The 'H=3d/H=5d improves gross' lever (+0.26 gross on PIT for the trend book, n=1) is assumed to transfer to a residual book; it has never been replicated.
